page: Microsoft Azure E8-2as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EASv4 server family. It runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and is powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor using the x86_64 architecture. The configuration features 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads, operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 32.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is provided via a 131 GB local SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPU resources are included.

Performance benchmarks reveal a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core CPU performance is strong, scoring 2693.59 in stress-ng tests, and single-threaded gzip compression and Geekbench single-core scores sit in the average tier. However, due to the low core count of 2 vCPUs, multi-core performance is constrained, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into the bottom tier. Memory bandwidth is also a notable bottleneck, with read-only small block bandwidth rated as poor at 128.45 GB/sec, and large block read and write speeds performing weakly.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers high memory density relative to its compute footprint, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel processing power. However, database operations and redis SET performance are benchmarked as poor, indicating that high-throughput transactional databases may experience bottlenecks. The server is best suited for memory-heavy, low-compute tasks, light caching layers, or specialized applications requiring large memory footprints with minimal CPU overhead.
